summary:
H.R. 8772, the "Legislative Branch Appropriations Act, 2025," is the annual appropriation measure funding the Legislative Branch for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2025. As reported by the House Committee on Appropriations (Rep. Valadao), it makes lump-sum and line-item appropriations across two titles and enacts several substantive amendments to standing law.

**Title I — Legislative Branch appropriations.** The bill funds the House of Representatives ($1,932,655,000 for salaries and expenses), including a $174,000 gratuity to Beatrice Y. Payne (widow of Rep. Donald M. Payne, Jr.); Members' Representational Allowances ($843,605,000); and multiple intern-compensation allowances established under 2 U.S.C. 5322a, 2 U.S.C. 5106, and section 113 of the Legislative Branch Appropriations Act, 2022 (Pub. L. 117-103). It appropriates $10,000,000 to the House Modernization Initiatives Account (2 U.S.C. 5513). Additional appropriations cover Joint Items, the Capitol Police (salaries $619,257,000; general expenses $213,158,000), the Office of Congressional Workplace Rights, CBO ($73,259,000), the Architect of the Capitol, the Library of Congress and its components, GPO, GAO ($896,700,000), and related entities.

**Substantive/administrative provisions.** Sec. 110 makes MRA funds available only for FY2025 and directs residual amounts to deficit or debt reduction. Sec. 111 caps vehicle-lease payments at $1,000/month. Sec. 113 amends section 303(f) of the Energy Policy Act of 1992 (42 U.S.C. 13212(f)) by striking House-specific alternative-fuel-vehicle acquisition provisions, effective FY2025 and thereafter. Sec. 114 amends section 312(d)(3) of the Legislative Branch Appropriations Act, 1992 (2 U.S.C. 2062(d)(3)) to permit payment of Center telecom expenses. Sec. 115 amends 5 U.S.C. 4120 to require Capitol Police Board approval for international training. Sec. 117 grants the Architect cooperative-agreement and plant-exchange authority.

**Title II — General provisions.** Sec. 202 imposes a fiscal-year obligation limitation absent express carryover. Sec. 206 limits interagency transfers. Sec. 209 prohibits procurement of covered telecommunications equipment (Huawei, ZTE, Hytera, Hikvision, Dahua, and foreign-adversary-connected entities per 10 U.S.C. 4872(d)), with staggered effective dates (FY2025 for (a)(1)(A); FY2026 for (a)(1)(B) and (b)(1)) and a one-time, two-year waiver. Sec. 210 exempts the GPO Director and Librarian from certain pay freezes. Sec. 211 amends 5 U.S.C. 13144 regarding fiduciary treatment of Member-provided medical care. Sec. 212 bars funding for specified diversity, equity, and inclusion training; Sec. 213 restricts "discriminatory action" against persons holding traditional-marriage beliefs, notwithstanding 1 U.S.C. 7 and 28 U.S.C. 1738C. Sec. 214 bars FY2025 Member COLA adjustments (2 U.S.C. 4501). Sec. 215 sets the spending-reduction account at $0.

These are appropriations, not merely authorizations, subject to the enumerated conditions and provisos.
